required_facts_checked.claim: A README functions as the landing page before readers inspect code.
The page serves peer reviewers, hiring teams, and the future maintainer.
The opening identifies the user, problem, and solution.
required_facts_checked.evidence: source: title and short description guidance

required_facts_checked.claim: A demo should show the core workflow early and can use a live link, video, GIF, screenshots, or sample I/O.
Evaluation documents datasets, cases, metrics, baselines, and improvements.
Testing should state available checks and limitations, including when there are no automated tests.
Monitoring names stored data and metrics used to diagnose failures.
A clean-machine quickstart includes prerequisites, dependencies, configuration, services, and start command.
Architecture, trade-offs, project structure, and limitations connect claims to implementation.
required_facts_checked.evidence: source: architecture, decisions, and limitations sections

substantive_edits: Revised the article as reader-facing guidance rather than a third-person account.
Preserved the README sequence from user/problem through demo, evidence, reproduction, architecture, and limitations.
Kept the testing limitation and trade-off reasoning explicit while removing redundant verdicts.
